_comment: Per-archetype layout ceilings. Read by scripts/lint-reels.mjs and importable by TS
(resolveJsonModule is on), so there is exactly one source of truth for what fits.
Numbers are in the 1080x1920 canvas space and are measured from the scene files, not
The camera scales the stage about transformOrigin 50% 55% (y=1056), so a nominal y
renders at 1056 + (y-1056)*zoom. `stageFloor` already accounts for this: 1330 renders
at ~1342 under the strongest push, leaving the caption zone clear.
The verdict is NOT subject to any of that. Since Phase 3 it is bottom-anchored at
band.verdictBottom (1462) and rendered outside the camera layer by SceneFrame, so the
only thing that can go wrong is wrapping to a third line. That is why this file no
Only scenes that content/reels.json can actually reach are listed. `fanout` exists in
src/scenes/DispatchFanout.tsx but Root.tsx has no branch for it yet, so adding it here
would let the linter pass a reel that renders as the wrong scene.
_narrationNote: bandHi was 68, calibrated on the original corpus. That corpus was written in a clipped
asyndetic style ('It files the ticket, updates the record, sends the email') which was
banned in STYLE-GUIDE 7c for sounding like copywriting rather than explanation.
Writing the same content with real connectives and named referents costs 10-15% more
words, so the band was raised to 82 rather than squeezing the prose back into the
style the band was measuring. hardMax and maxSeconds are unchanged: those are real
ceilings (Shorts length), where bandHi is only a house-style guide.

chain.note: Geometry adapts to step count — 2/3/4 steps get their own box height and gap so the last one always lands on stageFloor.

fill.note: Row pitch adapts so the box always looks filled: 3 tall rows or 5 short ones.

fanout.note: Worker box and spacing adapt to count: 340/306/248px pitch for 2/3/4. At four, outer edges land at x63 and x1017.

code.note: Mono is a flat 0.6em advance, so code lines are checked by exact character count against the 920px card, not estimated.

layers.note: Tier height adapts so the column bottom always lands on stageFloor. `note` is only rendered at 4 tiers or fewer, where the row is tall enough.

loop.note: The closing edge (last node back to the first) draws bold and late, and the camera frames it. That edge is the clip. Keep edge labels to ~2 words — they sit in the gaps between nodes, and those gaps are small on a 4-node ring.

gather.note: Three tiers, not a mirrored fanout — the argument lives in the middle collector. One brace carries the group label rather than N arrows repeating it.

nest.note: `direction` inverts the argument and the camera from one field: 'in' narrows and dims, 'out' widens and holds. Two clips using it opposite ways do not read as the same video.

matrix.note: The most reading of any archetype. Budget it — see W-MATRIX-BUDGET. Cells want 3 words, not a sentence.
